name: Tooltip
purpose: Reveals a short, non-interactive text label for whatever it wraps, on hover or keyboard focus — identifies an ambiguous control (an icon-only button, an avatar) without adding permanent visible text.
neverUseFor: Interactive content (links, buttons) inside the popup — use Popover/Menu instead; Tooltip is read-only text
Critical information the user must see — a tooltip can be missed entirely (no hover, no focus) and must never be the only way to learn something required to complete a task
Long-form help text or instructions — keep it to a short phrase; use a Popover or inline description for anything longer
rationale: Tooltip is a read-only text label shown on hover or focus and linked through aria-describedby (ADR-008), with auto-placement handled by ADR-009 and a 240px max width. It's one of the floating surfaces allowed a shadow (ADR-005), and it can never be the only way to learn required information.

mayExtendLocally: Write the label text and choose a preferred placement
mustEscalateToDS: Putting interactive content (links, buttons) inside a tooltip
Changing max width, delays or the placement engine
Using Tooltip for long-form help or critical information

authored.name: expanded
authored.description: Content is visible — driven by :hover/:focus-within by default, or forced via the `expanded` prop for a controlled/always-visible case (e.g. a preview).
authored.aria: handled by aria-describedby presence, not aria-expanded — a tooltip is a description, not a disclosure

anatomy.description: Position-relative wrapper around the trigger content (`children`).
The popup itself — role="tooltip", positioned via `placement`, referenced from the root via aria-describedby.

props.name: label
props.description: The tooltip's text content — short, plain text only, no interactive content.

props.name: children
props.description: The trigger — whatever the tooltip describes (an icon, an avatar, an icon-only button).

props.name: placement
props.description: Preferred side of the trigger. Tooltip auto-flips to the opposite side (and clamps sideways) on its own if the preferred side would clip the viewport — this is a starting preference, not a guarantee (see ADR-009, amending ADR-008).

props.name: expanded
props.description: Forces the content visible regardless of hover/focus — for a controlled/always-shown case. Leave unset for the normal hover/focus-driven behavior.

modes.hug: Width shrinks to the label's content, up to a max-width where it wraps.

width.note: Height is likewise content-driven (one or a few wrapped lines) — no fixed rung on the shared size scale, unlike Input/Select/Button.

a11y.role: tooltip (on tooltip-content), referenced from the trigger via aria-describedby
keyboardNav: Tab — focuses the trigger, showing the tooltip
Escape — dismisses while the trigger is focused

focus.note: focus is drawn by IconButton — see their a11y.applied.focus

motion: CSS transitions/animations: neutralised by the global prefers-reduced-motion rule

properties.name: children
properties.description: The trigger slot: any component (IconButton by default).

figma.structure: tooltip-root (auto layout,  4px = spacing/component/xs) > tooltip-trigger (children slot) + tooltip-content (the bubble: fill/inverse,  Caption / Regular,  radius/s,  shadow / s) on the placement side. No arrow,  like code.
figma.variantCombinations: 5 variants (2026-10-21,  owner-approved): placement top/bottom/left/right with expanded=true,  plus expanded=false once (the trigger alone).

children.reason: the trigger is a slot: an INSTANCE_SWAP lets the designer put any component under the tooltip (owner's request)

expanded.reason: unlike the other overlays,  a tooltip is drawn next to its trigger,  so showing or hiding it is a real look (owner's request)

KeyboardFocus.reason: keyboard focus on the trigger shows the tooltip; the trigger draws its own focus
